question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.
Tom was __standing besides the schoolhouse poster__, when the ball rolled towards him.
solution:
The correct answer is '**standing beside the schoolhouse poster**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The verb "**standing beside**" is the correct progressive tense form to describe an ongoing action in the past.
 
• The sentence describes an action that was happening at a specific time in the past ("**when the ball rolled towards him**"), so the progressive tense is appropriate.
 
• **Option 1** ("stand beside") and **Option 2** ("stood beside") are incorrect as they do not indicate an ongoing action.
 
• **No improvement** is incorrect because the highlighted segment ("besides") is grammatically incorrect and needs substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Tom was **standing beside the schoolhouse poster**__, when the ball rolled towards him."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "stand beside the schoolhouse poster"** is incorrect because it uses the base form of the verb "stand" instead of the correct progressive form.
 
• **Option 2: "stood beside the schoolhouse poster"** is incorrect because it does not indicate an ongoing action.
 
• **Option 4: "No improvement"** is incorrect because "besides" is a grammatical error and must be replaced with "beside."
